study_identification_part.si4_title: Regional, circuit and network heterogeneity of brain abnormalities in psychiatric disorders

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The abstract and introduction clearly state the aim to characterize individual heterogeneity of GMV differences across six psychiatric disorders and to map how heterogeneous regional deviations relate to common functional circuits and networks. This directly states research questions and the purpose of normative modeling.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: Here we present a comprehensive, multiscale characterization of the heterogeneity of gray matter volume (GMV) differences ... Normative models indicated that person-specific deviations ... were highly heterogeneous ... However, these deviations were embedded within common functional circuits and networks ...

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: Eligibility and quality criteria for the healthy reference cohort are described: HCs are defined as individuals without any clinical diagnosis; stringent image QC was performed (visual inspection, CAT12 IQR > 2.8 exclusion, pipeline failures); additional exclusions enforced age range 18–64, required complete demographics, and site/sex cell counts (exclude cells with <10 HCs and exclude sites below thresholds). Final HC sample size is reported with reasons for exclusion and counts.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: HCs; defined as the absence of any clinical diagnosis ... All T1-weighted images were visually inspected ... excluded 153 images with an IQR >2.8 ... An additional 63 images were excluded due to a failure of our processing pipeline ... We therefore excluded data cells containing less than ten HCs for a particular sex at a given site ... Our final sample available for analysis thus comprised 1,465 HCs and 1,294 cases.

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age, sex, and site are explicitly modeled as covariates via hierarchical Bayesian regression with random effects and partial pooling to address multisite variance, thereby handling site effects appropriately.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: We then trained a normative model based on hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) ... to establish a normative GMV range given an individual's age, sex and scan site ... we built our normative model using HBR ... estimating different but connected mean and variance components through shared prior distributions across sites ... The HBRs modelled site and sex effects with random slopes, intercepts and noise, to model GMV as a function of age, sex and site ...

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: Data sources for the healthy cohort are described and linked, including ABIDE I/II, ASRB, HCP and other datasets; the paper states no new data were collected and points to dataset references.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: This study used neuroimaging data collected across multiple independent datasets ... ABIDE I and ABIDE II ... ASRB ... Human Connectome Project (HCP) ... No new data were collected for this manuscript.

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: Secondary data from existing datasets were used; per guide, acquisition protocol is not applicable for secondary data. The paper states no new data were collected and refers to Supplementary Table 1 for acquisition parameters.
nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.supporting_text: No new data were collected for this manuscript. Image acquisition parameters for each dataset are provided in Supplementary Table 1.

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing is described in detail: CAT12 VBM pipeline in SPM12/MATLAB, DARTEL normalization to MNI space, bias-field correction, modulation, voxel inclusion threshold; code references provided.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: Regional GMV was estimated using the CAT12 VBM pipeline ... included as an extension of SPM v7771 in MATLAB v9.8 ... scans were normalized into standard MNI IXI555 space ... images were bias-field corrected and modulated ... retained voxels with a tissue probability ≥0.2.

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The study used a held-out HC test set and five-fold cross-validation within HC train to assess generalization and model fit, satisfying internal validation requirements.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: The test data (HC test) ... comprised the 10% of HCs ... completely independent of the normative model ... To assess model generalizability, we used five-fold cross-validation applied to the HC train cohort ...

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The paper does not report applying the trained normative model to an independent external healthy dataset beyond the held-out HC test partition derived from the same multisite pool. No separate external HC dataset evaluation is described.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: The test data (HC test) ... comprised the 10% of HCs from sites with ≥30 HCs ... completely independent of the normative model ...

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The statistical approach is described: region-wise hierarchical Bayesian regression using PCNtoolkit (v0.16), Box-Cox transformation, modeling of site and sex with random effects and shared priors; z-score formulation and thresholding are specified.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: We used normative modeling ... PCNtoolkit v0.16 ... we built our normative model using HBR ... shared prior distributions across sites ... HBRs modelled site and sex effects with random slopes, intercepts and noise ... we generated deviation z maps ... thresholded the deviation maps at z > |2.6| ...

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: Model performance metrics are reported, including explained variance, mean standardized log-loss, and standardized mean squared error across regions, presented for CV folds and test cohort.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: Performance metrics for the normative models. These metrics measure the accuracy ... distributions of i) explained variance (EXPV; higher is better), ii) Mean standardized log-loss (MSLL; lower is better), and iii) Standardized mean squared error (SMSE; lower is better) ... The top five rows present data from each cross-validation fold. The bottom row presents data for the test cohort.

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: HC train and HC test partition sizes and demographics are reported: HC train n=1,196 (55% male); HC test n=269 (52% male; age range 18–62).
nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.supporting_text: ... training set comprising 1,196 HCs (55.02% male; Fig. 2a; HC train) ... The remaining 269 controls (52.04% male; age range 18-62 years) were held out as a test set (HC test) ...

cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.reason: For secondary datasets, the paper cites DSM/ICD diagnostic criteria, describes uniform image QC and additional exclusions (age 18–64, missing demographics/clinical info, site/sex cell counts), and reports final sample sizes with reasons for exclusion.
cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: Our cases were diagnosed according to Diagnostic Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM) or the International Classification of Diseases (ICD) criteria ... All T1-weighted images were visually inspected ... excluded 153 images with an IQR > 2.8 ... excluded participants if they were below 18 years or above 64 years of age ... or if the data came from a site with less than ten individuals ... Our final sample available for analysis thus comprised 1,465 HCs and 1,294 cases.

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.reason: The study explicitly states that investigating relationships with symptom profiles and other clinical variables (e.g., medication status, illness duration, disease severity) was beyond scope and not conducted.
cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: ... investigating correlations with symptom profiles or other clinically relevant variables such as age of onset, illness duration, medication exposure or disease severity across disorders was beyond our scope.

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: The paper defines deviation z-scores and their direction (negative/positive GMV deviations), reports a quantitative threshold (|z| > 2.6) to define extreme deviations, and discusses clinical relevance at circuit/network levels. However, explicit clinical interpretation linking deviation magnitudes to symptoms is noted as beyond the scope.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: ... calculate a z score ... which quantifies the extent to which an individual's regional GMV estimate deviates from the model prediction ... We thresholded the deviation maps at z > |2.6| ... we first focus on characterizing negative GMV deviations ... before considering positive GMV deviations ... our hierarchical Bayesian model ... investigating correlations with symptom profiles ... was beyond our scope.
